stem: In a code language, CHAIR is written as EJCKT. Using the same code, what does FKOOR stand for in plain English?

per_option_rationale.rationale: The encoding shifts each letter +2 (C->E, H->J, A->C, I->K, R->T). Decoding reverses with -2: F(6)->D(4), K(11)->I(9), O(15)->M(13), O(15)->M(13), R(18)->P(16), giving DIMMP.
FLOOR is what you get if no decoding shift is applied - treating the coded word as already plain text, which ignores the +2 rule entirely.
An arithmetic slip on the last letter makes R(18)-2 = 15 = O instead of the correct 16 = P, producing FLOOM.
Misreading K as J (one letter off) gives K(11)-2 = I correct but the misread makes it J-2 = H, and combining with other small slips yields DILMP.

explanation: The rule shifts each letter forward by 2 in the alphabet (C->E, H->J, A->C, I->K, R->T). To decode FKOOR, subtract 2 from each: F->D, K->I, O->M, O->M, R->P, giving DIMMP.

explanation_sections.punchline: Identify the uniform +2 shift from the given pair, confirm it on all five letters, then subtract 2 to decode.
explanation_sections.approach: Deductive trace: compute the shift for each letter pair - C->E (+2), H->J (+2), A->C (+2), I->K (+2), R->T (+2). Uniform +2 confirmed. Apply -2 to each letter of FKOOR: F(6)->D(4), K(11)->I(9), O(15)->M(13), O(15)->M(13), R(18)->P(16).
explanation_sections.lesson: Always verify the shift on every letter of the given example before decoding; a uniform shift that holds for all five letters is reliable.
explanation_sections.timing: About 50-60 seconds. Fastest elimination: FLOOR requires zero shift - rule it out immediately since a shift exists.
